title: Adaptive Batch Safeguard: prober-driven fingerprinting, heuristic scoring, and roll-forward planner
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a conservative, measurable recommendation engine that suggests continuous batching and cache policies per workload fingerprint. The engine must: (1) derive compact workload fingerprints from runtime telemetry (latency percentiles, token lengths, KV hit ratios, request inter-arrival distribution), (2) compute a heuristic score balancing cost savings vs latency/regression risk, and (3) provide a safe apply/rollforward plan (shadow->canary->gradual->rollback) with automatic rollback triggers. Focus is on minimizing false positives that would increase p99 latency or error rates while still surfacing meaningful cost reductions.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint extractor produces deterministic 128-bit IDs for observed workload buckets with <1% collision in synthetic tests
Heuristic score maps to one of three recommended actions: no-change / conservative-coalescence / aggressive-coalescence

Safe-apply plan can be executed by the infra API: shadow apply (no impact), canary (1% traffic), gradual ramp (1->30% over 2 hours) with automatic rollback on latency degradations >10% p99 or error increase >0.5%
Staging e2e tests demonstrate cost reduction signal for a representative microburst workload with no p95/p99 regressions across 10 test runs
Runbook and rollout CLI steps documented and linked in design doc
notes: 2026-02-28 - Initial scope drafted after cost-sprint retrospective; goal set to create automated recommendations rather than forced config changes
2026-03-02 - Telemetry schema PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/prs/telemetry-schema#134 (proto and exporter changes). Decided to add per-request KV cache hit fields to enable accurate scoring

2026-03-04 - Prototype fingerprint encoder implemented in Go (service: batch-prober). PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prs/batch-prober#27. Encoder uses bloom-filtered token-length histogram + inter-arrival sketch
2026-03-05 - Design review with PM & Design. Trade-off: compact fingerprints vs cardinality loss. Consensus: use hierarchical fingerprint buckets (coarse->fine) to allow safe global recommendations
2026-03-08 - Safety thresholds discussion: conservative defaults adopted to prioritize latency SLOs. Product requested an opt-in aggressive mode for dedicated customers
2026-03-10 - Shadow apply flow validated in staging. Canary plumbing implemented in infra-runner service and CLI. End-to-end tests added to CI (integration tests run nightly)
2026-03-12 - Blocker discovered: high-cardinality KV cache metric ingestion causing backend index explosion in telemetry-store. Task created (ENG-863210) to add cardinality limits and retention rules
